screening.reason: Reports a mega- and meta-analysis of ABIDE I+II resting-state fMRI connectome dynamics comparing ASD vs HC, with SRS-score prediction; satisfies inclusion 1-4.

evidence_spans.text: we conducted mega- and meta-analyses of resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging data of 939 participants (440 ASD patients and 499 healthy controls, all males) from 18 independent sites, selected from the ABIDE (Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange) dataset.
evidence_spans.claim: Study mega/meta-analyzed rsfMRI connectome dynamics in 939 ABIDE participants (440 ASD, 499 HC) from 18 sites.

evidence_spans.text: had maximal head motion of less than 5 mm and 5 degrees, and mean framewise displacement (FD) (1) of less than 0.5 mm
evidence_spans.claim: QC excluded scans with head motion >5mm/5deg or mean FD >0.5mm.

evidence_spans.text: Thus, after all selection criteria had been applied, we obtained a dataset consisting of scans from 939 participants (ASD/HC, 440/499) taken from 18 different sites
evidence_spans.claim: Final analysed cohort was 939 participants (440 ASD/499 HC) across 18 sites after QC.

evidence_spans.text: All rsfMRI data were preprocessed with a standardized and harmonized pipeline using the GRETNA package (36).
evidence_spans.claim: Preprocessing used the GRETNA package pipeline.

evidence_spans.text: network nodes were defined as 512 regions of interest with uniform areas obtained from a random parcellation (38)
evidence_spans.claim: Dynamic connectomes used a 512-node random parcellation.

evidence_spans.text: the ASD group showed a higher mean value (Cohen’s d = .18, p = .007) and a lower standard deviation (Cohen’s d = -.19, p = .004) in whole-brain modular variability than the HC group
evidence_spans.claim: ASD showed higher mean and lower SD of whole-brain modular variability than HC (Cohen's d=.18 and -.19).

evidence_spans.text: the ASD group showed higher modular variability mainly in several default-mode regions, including the medial prefrontal cortex, posterior cingulate gyrus, and angular gyrus (Cohen’s d ranging from .19 to .33), and lower variability primarily in the visual cortex (Cohen’s d ranging from -.24 to -.19) (FDR corrected p < .05)
evidence_spans.claim: ASD showed higher modular variability in default-mode regions and lower variability in visual cortex vs HC (FDR p<.05).

evidence_spans.text: we found that brain dynamics was a significant predictor of SRS scores (r = .16, pperm = .002)
evidence_spans.claim: Brain modular dynamics significantly predicted SRS social-impairment scores (r=.16, pperm=.002).

evidence_spans.text: We performed a leave-one-site-out cross-validation to assess whether our main findings were biased by site specific sites.
evidence_spans.claim: Robustness of group differences was assessed with leave-one-site-out cross-validation.

charting.title: Alterations in Connectome Dynamics in Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Harmonized Mega- and Meta-analysis Study Using the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange Dataset
charting.primary_goal: Characterise ASD-vs-HC alterations in resting-state dynamic connectome modular structure and link them to social-impairment severity and gene expression.
charting.task_type: Resting-state (eyes open/closed as per site protocol, not further specified)
charting.diagnosis_assessment: ABIDE site clinical diagnosis; ADOS-2 and ADI-R scores reported for characterization
charting.age_range: 5-35 years (initial ABIDE range before age<35 restriction)
charting.medications_therapies: Medicated ASD individuals were not excluded (limited medication information available from ABIDE)
charting.age_matched: No significant age difference between ASD and HC (p = .84)
charting.specific_features: Modular variability of dynamic brain connectomes (512-node random parcellation, sliding-window multilayer network model)
charting.importance_method: Frequency of nodal selection as a feature during LOOCV
charting.top_features_identified: Medial prefrontal cortex and visual cortex nodes made the largest contribution to SRS prediction
charting.feature_change_direction: Higher modular variability in ASD in default-mode regions (medial prefrontal cortex, posterior cingulate, angular gyrus); lower modular variability in ASD in visual cortex
charting.specific_algorithms: Support vector regression (LIBSVM) predicting SRS score from whole-brain modular variability maps
charting.validation_methodology: Leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) for SRS prediction; leave-one-site-out cross-validation as a sensitivity analysis for group differences
charting.performance_metrics: Correlation (r) between predicted and actual SRS scores, permutation test
charting.key_performance_results: we found that brain dynamics was a significant predictor of SRS scores (r = .16, pperm = .002)
charting.summary_key_findings: ASD showed higher mean and lower variance of whole-brain dynamic modular variability than HC, with regionally higher variability in default-mode regions and lower variability in visual cortex; modular variability predicted SRS social-impairment severity and correlated with ASD-risk gene expression patterns.
charting.features_associated_disorder: Dynamic modular variability in default-mode network regions (higher in ASD) and visual cortex (lower in ASD)
charting.future_directions_recommended: Extend to female participants and other age ranges; incorporate ASD-specific (not only healthy) gene expression data when available.

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Mega- and meta-analysis (associational) plus SVR prediction of SRS severity; ABIDE I+II, 939 participants (440 ASD/499 HC, all male), 18 sites
narrative_row.methods: GRETNA-preprocessed rsfMRI, sliding-window dynamic connectomes (512-node random parcellation), multilayer-Louvain modular variability, GAM mega-analysis with ComBat site harmonisation and FDR correction, site-wise meta-analysis, SVR/LOOCV prediction of SRS scores, Allen Human Brain Atlas transcriptome association.
narrative_row.outcomes: ASD showed higher mean / lower SD of whole-brain modular variability than HC; regionally higher variability in default-mode regions and lower in visual cortex (FDR p<.05); modular variability predicted SRS scores (r=.16, pperm=.002); alterations correlated with ASD-risk gene expression.
narrative_row.key_limitations: Male-only sample; gene expression reference from only 5 healthy post-mortem brains; medicated individuals not excluded; cross-sectional.
narrative_row.relevance_notes: Detailed, numerically explicit ABIDE I+II QC pipeline (motion, scan length, IQ, age, site size) giving a reconstructible cohort definition; demonstrates site-harmonised mega-analysis plus leave-one-site-out sensitivity check as a model for site handling.
